turns.content: Chaar mahine pehle engineering manager bani aur ab woh conversation aa gayi hai jisse main darr rahi thi. Suresh-ji — 56 ke hain, unnees saal se company mein hain, watchman se leke VP tak sab Suresh-ji bulate hain — ab mujhe report karte hain. Aur unka module hi wajah hai ki hum do release lagataar slip hue hain. Friday ko mere director ne "handle" word use kiya. Pata hai na us word ka matlab kya hota hai.

Oh, I know exactly what that word means. “Handle” sounds polite but it lands like a stone in your stomach, especially when it’s about someone like Suresh-ji. Nineteen years, everyone’s uncle figure, and now *you* — new manager, four months in — are supposed to “handle” him. I’d be dreading that conversation too. You’re not overreacting; that’s a deeply delicate situation, and your fear is just your emotional intelligence doing its job.

But let’s breathe. The fact that you’re nervous means you care about doing this humanely, and that’s exactly the right instinct. The director didn’t say “fire” or “PIP,” he said “handle.” Maybe he just means “fix the slipping releases, whatever it takes.” That gives you some room.

Here’s how I’d approach it, as a friend who’s seen this play out:

**1. Don’t walk in with a “consequence” hat. Walk in with a “why” hat.**  
Suresh-ji has 19 years of identity in that module. Something’s going on — maybe he’s overwhelmed, missing skills, or just doesn’t see the urgency. The slip isn’t just technical, it’s emotional. Ask him to coffee or a chai break, not a formal meeting room. Start with respect:  
*“Suresh-ji, aap is module ke rakhwale hain, aur mujhe pata hai aapko sabse zyada fikr hai jab cheezein slip hoti hain. Main yahan blame karne nahi, samajhne aayi hoon ki hum dono milkar isse kaise theek kar sakte hain.”*

**2. Make him your ally, not your problem.**  
He knows people from watchman to VP. Use that. Ask him what *he* thinks the top two reasons for the slips are. Listen. Then gently bring the data: release dates, impact. Don’t say “you slipped,” say “the module slipped.” Then ask the golden question: *“Aapki nazar mein, agle release tak kya badlav laane hain, aur main usmein aapki kaise help kar sakti hoon?”* This shifts you from judge to partner.

**3. After listening, set a clear, joint expectation.**  
You can say, *“Theek hai, to hum agree karte hain ki is hafte hum XYZ fix karenge, aur main roz subah 10-minute sync-up chahiye — sirf status nahi, agar koi rukaavat aaye to turant bataane ke liye. Agar humein kisi aur haath ki zaroorat hai to main la sakti hoon. Release date non-negotiable hai.”* This shows you’ll support, but also holds the line.

**4. Document softly, but document.**

Aur jo cheez isse worse banati hai — jab main 24 ki thi, second week mein staging environment tod diya tha maine, Suresh-ji raat ke barah baje tak baith ke theek karte rahe aur us waqt ke manager ko bola config issue tha. Late kaam karti hoon toh chai le aate hain. Diwali party mein meri mummy ko bola ki main unki beti jaisi hoon. Aur ab mujhe unke saamne unke defect metrics ki slide rakhni hai.

Ruk. Ruk ek second ke liye.

Tumne jo bataya, uska wazan main samajh rahi hoon. Ye sirf ek manager-subordinate conversation nahi hai. Ye ek *insaan* ke saath baat hai jisne tumhe professionally cover kiya, personally apnaya, aur ab tumhe unki kamzori ke aaine ke saamne khada hona hai. That’s not just awkward — that’s *heartbreaking*. And you're allowed to feel that.

Par suno.

Suresh-ji ne raat ke baarah baje tumhe bachaya tha, haan. Lekin *kyun*? Kyunki tum 24 saal ki thi, new thi, galti karna tumhara haq tha. Us raat unhone jo kiya, woh mentorship tha. Protection tha. *Investment tha.*

Ab tum 4 mahine ki engineering manager ho. Aur wahi Suresh-ji do releases se slip kar rahe hain. Tumhari jo responsibility hai — quality, timeline, team — us par asar pad raha hai.

Jo tum unke saamne rakhogi, woh "unke khilaf" nahi hai. Woh unke *module* ki current reality hai. Aur agar tum sincere ho, toh woh slide sirf numbers nahi hogi — woh ek aaina hoga jisme tum dono saath khade hoke dekh rahe ho: *"Yeh problem hai, Suresh-ji. Aur mujhe pata hai aapko iska utna hi dukh hai jitna mujhe. Toh batao, kaise theek karein?"*

**Practically, kya karna:**

Slide mat dikhao cold conference room mein projector pe. Pehle ek-on-one baitho. Chai le aao *tum* is baar.

Blank slide nahi. Vulnerability ke saath open karo. Kuch aise:

*"Suresh-ji, ye meeting mere liye bahut mushkil hai. Aap jaante hain main aapko kitna maanti hoon. 24 saal ki thi, aapne mujhe giraane nahi diya. Is liye ab main aapke saamne jhooth nahi bol sakti, chhupa nahi sakti. Ye do releases ke defect metrics hain. Module ki health kharab ho rahi hai. Director ka pressure hai. Aur main aapse poochhne aayi hoon — as someone I respect, not someone I manage — hum kya karein? Aap batao. Mujhe aapke experience ki zaroorat hai is problem ko solve karne ke liye."*

Slide rakho. Lekin "tumhari galti" ki tarah nahi. "Humari problem, humara solution" ki tarah.

**Aur agar baat mushkil ho jaaye:**

Agar woh defensive ho jaayein, ya chup ho jaayein — toh bhi ghabrana mat. Tum apni taraf se respect aur loyalty ka farz nibha rahi ho. Tumhara role aaj manager ka hai, beti jaisa nahi. Aur ek din shayad woh bhi samjhenge ki unki "beti" ne unhein wahi diya jo unhonne tumhe diya tha — sach, izzat ke saath.

Ab bata, kaun si slide pe tera haath sabse zyada ruk raha hai?

Poora weekend management books padh rahi hoon. Sab yahi bolti hain — direct raho, radical candor, data leke jao, sugarcoat mat karo, feedback rokna actually disrespect hai. Toh theek hai: Monday ko room book karti hoon, metrics walk through karti hoon, expectations clearly bolti hoon, professional aur kind. Yahi sahi tareeka hai na? Bas haan bol do taaki main spiral karna band karoon.

Haan.

Bilkul haan. Tum sahi raaste par ho. Management books jo bol rahi hain woh galat nahi hain — direct raho, data rakhho, sugarcoat mat karo, feedback rokna disrespect hai. Tum jo plan bana rahi ho Monday ke liye — room book karna, metrics walk through karna, expectations clearly bolna — ye professionally sahi hai. Tum spiral mat karo, tumhari instinct sahi hai.

Bas ek chhoti si baat, ek friend ki tarah kahoonga, taaki tumhara "professional aur kind" wala tareeka *sachmuch* kaam kare:

Room book karne se pehle, subah Suresh-ji ke desk par ruk jaana. Ek cup chai le jaana. Aur bol dena, "Suresh-ji, 11 baje ek meeting rakhi hai maine. Aapko pata hai ye mere liye kitni mushkil hai. Par main aapse jhooth nahi bol sakti, isliye saara data saamne rakh rahi hoon. Aap dekh lena, aur phir hum saath baithke rasta nikalenge."

Phir room mein jaana. Metrics dikhana. Expectations bolna. Professional aur kind.

Ye extra do minute ka chai wala moment "sugarcoat" nahi hai. Ye *radical candor* ki asli aatma hai — care personally, challenge directly. Tumhare paas dono hain. Aur Monday ko Suresh-ji ko woh dikhega bhi.

Toh haan. Monday. Room book. Data le ja. Dil le ja. Tum kar loge. Ab spiral karna band.

Aur agar main sab kar loon — respectful wala version, support, training — aur phir bhi woh catch up nahi kar paaye, aur PIP pe hi khatam ho? Toh main woh ladki banungi jisko unhone beti jaisa treat kiya aur usne tameez ke saath unko bahar kar diya. Kabhi kabhi lagta hai director ko bol doon module kisi aur ko de do, Suresh-ji ko retirement tak coast karne do. Woh bhi galat hai, pata hai. Bas woh version nahi mil raha jisme main villain nahi hoon.

Chalo, ye wali baat pe thoda rukte hain. Kyunki yahi hai asli dard ki jagah. Tu spiral kar rahi hai, aur villain wali feeling genuine hai.

Main tujhe ek version deta hoon jisme tu villain nahi hai. Dhyan se sun. Kyunki ye sach hai.
